title: What are we shaping?
question: Shape writes a confirmed UX/UI brief, then stops — no code. PRODUCT.md and Functional Clarity (DESIGN.md) already exist, so this is not a rebrand unless you say so. Which surface should the brief cover? Use the note for a different route, a new feature, or if this is actually a visual-world replacement.

options.label: Landing / waitlist
options.thesis: A first-time visitor must understand the handshake, want in, and join the waitlist — without a feed costume.
options.body: Anonymous SSR marketing, logo-first hero, playground, About, waitlist. Primary audience is people who have not joined yet. Operator proof stays off this page (Enterprise is a link).
options.case: Usual first surface for a full upgrade. Mode: Persuade.

options.label: Personal dashboard
options.thesis: Someone who already connected in the room continues that relationship: Memory Box, map, chat, QR, calls.
options.body: Post-handshake companion. Success is continuing a real connection, not lingering. Hardware handshake stays on the phone.
options.case: Mode: Operate. Inherits Functional Clarity; composition may still be open.

options.label: Click for Business
options.thesis: A venue or promoter must see who actually showed up together — verified factions, not door counts.
options.body: Heatmap, tribes, vibe radar, sticky score, events engagement. Anonymized topology. Consumer chrome stays out of the way.

options.label: Public events
options.thesis: Find, understand, and RSVP to a real night — guest-friendly, no account required on the microsite.
options.body: Directory, create, /e/{id} guest RSVP, Source Serif titles, CardVisual covers. Mix of public conversion and operator publishing.
options.case: Mode depends on the exact route you name in the note.
